page.layout: One text page with marginal notes in the right margin. Full-width running text in one column, with a decorative rule below the paragraph about the seven classes, then the chapter heading and the text of Cap. 11 below it. Notes stand in the right margin beside the paragraphs they accompany. Signature "Ee 5" at the foot.

p.i: Hujusmodi typos & Calendaria semper in conspectu in Musæis suis habeant studiosi, & innovent subinde secundùm intervalla trium, quatuor, aut ad summum sex mensium. Vide Consiliarium nostrum Academicum, ubi prolixè tradidimus architecturam & usum typorum, & Calendariorum.

main_text.p: Ordo librorum est eorum ad facilem inventionem & conservationem collocatio in loco editiori atq; amœniori.III.Ordo librorum.

p.i: Communior librorum dispositio solet esse eorum in septem classes distributio.

main_text.p: Prima classis contineat scripta Theologica, juxta Theologia divisionem. Secunda, philosophica, juxta philosophiæ divisionem, supra à nobis traditam. Tertia, Medica. Quarta, Juridica. Quinta, historica. Sexta, Oratoria & Poetica, adeoq; critica & philologica. Septima, Encyclia sive universalia. Aliter partitur classes librorum Joannes Mabuenus in Roseto spiritali.
main_text.head: Cap. 11. De examine ingeniorum, sive arte prænoscendi ingenia.

p.i: Quot corporum sunt formæ, tot ingeniorum; quorum examen paucis trademus, adeoq; artem prænoscendi ingenia ptascribemus[?].

main_text.p: Plato ad tres causas refert ingeniorum diversitatem: ad humanam, naturalem, & divinam. Humana, ut lex, educatio, consuetudo diversa. Naturalis, elementorum atq; alimentorum varietas. Divina, siderum atq; Dei potestas. Sed hanc sententiam non facimus nostram. Videat, qui volet, in hanc senten-Unde varietas ingeniorum juxta Platonem.

page.notes: The decorative rule between the paragraph on the seven classes and the chapter heading is an ornament, not text, and is not transcribed. The first paragraph has no indent and is treated as continuing from the previous page. The page number is printed as "441" (the final digit is set in old type). The italic and roman distinctions in the list of classes are read from the scan and may not be exact. "ptascribemus" is doubtful; the printed letters "pt" are unclear. The sentence "Videat, qui volet, in hanc senten-" continues on the next page. The printed note "Naturalis, Platonem." beside the Plato paragraph is read as part of the note "Unde varietas ingeniorum juxta Platonem."
